item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.
